top_choice_rationale: Base editing is a chemical mechanism turned into a controllable capability: a deaminase, including the laboratory-evolved TadA adenine deaminase that had no known DNA activity, is directed to one base without a double-strand break. It is reproduced widely and in early clinical use. As a single part, Liu, Komor and Gaudelli cover the conception and both first demonstrated editor classes within three names. Remaining risks are the Kondo and Nishida claim, ten-year maturity, and proximity to the 2020 prize. Other proposals rank below because they either drop Komor and Gaudelli to fit a second part whose attribution is contested (Crews and Handa omit Deshaies and Ciulli; C-N coupling must be distinguished from the 2010 prize), or lack comparably sharp first-demonstration evidence.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, whose candidates are not in P004
